thread:
anita: Heads-up: starting bring-up for janus-embed-smallv2 (6.5B) — want quick sanity checks on recall@1/5 and cluster stability before we roll to staging. will run int8 per-channel and fp16 baselines. @kevin @sam
kevin: sg. what dataset? short queries or long? can you post eval command?
anita: short queries + wiki-k10 holdout. eval command: ```./tools/eval_embeddings --model janus-embed-smallv2 --quant int8_perchannel --holdout wiki_k10 --k 1,5 --batch 128 --seed 42```
sam: got it. running now on batch of 10k. ping if you want me to run fp16 too
eval-bot: Eval job started: job_id=job_2026_03_21_01
Estimated finish: ~8m
lucas: quick question: are we using cosine or inner-product? config shows cosine. that affects recall numbers.
anita: cosine. will try ip too if we see odd results.
sam: first glance: int8 per-channel recall@1 dropped from 0.72->0.65 vs fp16 baseline on short queries. recall@5 dropped 0.92->0.88. numbers preliminary.
kevin: hmm 0.65 is sizable. any cluster shifts? t-SNE/UMAP looks different?
sam: sending small screenshot to #eng-ml (not in thread). but cluster centroids seem elongated, more overlap between topic clusters.
anita: can you paste nearest neighbor example for a failing query? `query: 'how to reset postgres password'`
sam: nn list (fp16 top3):
1) 'reset postgres password' (0.98)
2) 'postgres password reset steps' (0.95)
3) 'pg_hba.conf and auth' (0.80)
int8 top3:
1) 'postgres user permissions' (0.88)
2) 'reset postgres password' (0.85)
3) 'pg_hba.conf and auth' (0.77)
lucas: looks like scalar shift in similarity margin. might be quant scale mismatch for token embeddings. can we try per-channel with symmetric vs asymmetric calibration? @sam can you rerun with quant_mode=asymmetric
sam: on it. rerunning: ```./tools/eval_embeddings --model janus-embed-smallv2 --quant int8_perchannel --quant_mode asymmetric --holdout wiki_k10 --k 1,5 --batch 128```
eval-bot: Eval job started: job_id=job_2026_03_21_02
Estimated finish: ~8m
anita: also try running with FP16+postnorm scaling: multiply embeddings by 1.15 before cosine. seems to sometimes compensate.
kevin: :thinking: if asymmetric improves recall then we should update quant profile in model registry and run full staging sweep.
sam: asymmetric run finished: recall@1 = 0.69, recall@5 = 0.90. improvement but still below fp16. centroids tighter.
anita: good. can you run a small ablation: disable layernorm folding and see effect? maybe folding introduced bias
sam: queued. will report numbers later. opening ticket to track: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-5432
lucas: also add a quick precision/recall per-class breakdown — some rare topics seem most affected.
anita: thanks everyone. next steps: sam finish ablation, kevin prep staging sweep if ablation helps, lucas do per-class analysis, i'll draft release notes about quant caveats. :thumbsup:
